_comment: Recorded budgets for a STOCK build of build/core/dos_core.elf. Checked by scripts/budget_gate.py; write with --update. RAISING A NUMBER HERE IS THE REVIEW -- the commit that raises it must say what grew and why. See scripts/common/budgets.py for what each one means and what the frame count is and is not.

SB DIRECT DAC (cmd 10h) IS RESAMPLED AT A STEADY RATE: sb_dac_render() reads the FIFO at an exponential mean of arrivals per output sample (1/8 per window for 64 windows, then 1/256), nudged by at most 3% in proportion to the queue's distance from two windows' worth, with linear interpolation; it used to spread each window's arrivals over that window. Console, Another World: runs as before, sb_dac_avg steady within 0.25%, queue 170-300 samples. Whether it SOUNDS right is the owner's to say: his recording of the old renderer had one sustained note between 661 and 684 Hz. A shrink costs the 0Dh card's second piece its contents, and KEEN4 took one at every level load. The sampler's history is also cleared by x86_pager_reset() (the next title's reserve was the last title's working set). RAM_EMU 0x24061DF0 -> 0x24061E38 (+72 B, 456 B below the step). THE 0Dh READ SHADOW IS REBUILT A GRANULE AT A TIME, ON ACCESS: a change of read state marks the sixteen 4 KB granules stale and points their fold entries at FOLD_INVALID; the first accesses to a granule get their bytes patched in place (24 per granule), a reader that keeps going gets the granule's sixteen pages rebuilt and its entry back. Read-modify-write trap stubs call x86_nor_slow_rmw (same size) so the latch record survives.
